_about: NapAttack's progression spine as data (Claude K, story and progression stream, 21 Oct 2026). What unlocks when, from the first launch to the moon Lumen: the ways that open the world (world-unlocks.md, PR #95; re-sited by the world plan v5.3 and Claude G's routeGates in lib/world-routes.ts), the regions and their rest spots, the eleven resident stories (text in stories.json), the fourteen folk, the outings, the home base's hearth (PR #146) and the comforts. Read by lib/progression.ts (typed loader and cross-checks, npm run check:progression) and by scripts/sim-progression.ts, which plays three resters through it on top of the C33 economy sim and writes docs/story/pacing.md. A PROPOSAL: nothing here is read by the game or changes a rule until Matt decides (docs/story/choices-for-matt.md). Real minutes and Dream Dust throughout.
decided: Either route opens each way: a rest task or Dream Dust; Dust chipped in comes back if the task opens it first; shortcuts and comforts are Dust only (Matt, 20 Oct ~01:25, #95)
At most one way opens a calendar day (Matt, 20 Oct ~01:25, #95)
Rests run in real time when unlocks ship; demo speed stays a developer switch (Matt, 20 Oct ~01:25, #95)
C9 first: Dream Dust can never be lost in raids before ways ship (Matt, 20 Oct ~01:25, #95)

You play a folk with your Grassling as familiar; 14 folk; every folk after the three starters is an apprentice who joins when their region's resident story ends; nothing expires, costs Dust or needs a fight win; no folk gates a place (Matt, 20 Oct 23:20 and 23:26, cast.md)
The world is arrangement A of the world plan v5 (Matt, 20 Oct 14:45); the rocket at the Launch Cape replaces the space elevator and Halcyon's lander goes on to Lumen (world plan decision 8)
The currency is Dream Dust (Matt, 20 Oct 21:29)

storyLinks.about: PROPOSAL (choices page): a way marked storyLink comes in reach only once its story has reached the given chapter, so each region's story opens the road onward and a region is lived in before the next one opens. Off, the road is #95's as Matt approved it in principle. The pacing page plays both.

chapter.about: Chapter 1 comes with the first rest at any of the region's rest spots. Each later chapter needs one more rest at the region's spots that ends on a later calendar day than the previous chapter, or is a long rest. One chapter per rest, and (PROPOSAL, like the ways) at most one new chapter in all on any calendar day, so every welcome-back has at most one story beat and stories stay spaced out however much someone rests. A chapter never waits on a date, never expires and is never lost; it is shown in the next welcome-back and kept in the journal. Chapter 3 ends the story: the apprentice asks to come along and joins at once.

spots.about: A rest spot is found by walking to it once (like a keepsake). From then on the NAP sheet and the map offer it as where the next rest happens; the companion goes there while the player is away, so nobody has to walk back. The hut's bed is the default. Every spot pays the same Dream Dust a minute (gameplay-regions G1 and G2, proposals).

reopen.about: PROPOSAL (lane R 16:29; choices item 13): after a rest the app opens where that rest happened (the hut's bed by default, so usually home, with the welcome-back sheet); opened without a rest in between, it opens where the player left off. Today it always opens in the garden while save.world still names the last place; the saved spot follows whichever is decided.

start.familiar: a Grassling, hatched at the first launch

othersJoin.about: PROPOSAL (cast.md: the first pick sticks; the other two join later through the stone circle): when Cairn wakes and the valley story ends, the circle calls the two valley folk not chosen, and they join together.

firstLaunch.what: Hatch a Grassling (it keeps the type: REST, ROAM or FOCUS) and choose one of three valley folk: Bramble, Puffcap or Velvet. Their stone in the woodland circle lights; the other two valley folk join when Cairn wakes.
firstLaunch.line: hello. i'm small, but i'm very good at naps.

firstLaunch.what: A short walk round the garden and the hut; the hut's bed is the first rest spot, and the valley's spots are found by walking past them (the spring pool, the millpond bench, the bandstand, the library, the ridge cabin).
firstLaunch.line: the bed's ours. want to see the village?

firstLaunch.what: The first rest (the NAP sheet suggests 10 minutes). It meets the first visitor (guaranteed, as today), meets W1's task (one rest of 10 minutes) so the Headland stile is mended, and brings the valley's chapter 1 (the gardener, and a mossy stone that turns to face the garden).
firstLaunch.line: while you were away, the shepherd mended the stile. and that stone moved. i'm sure of it.

firstLaunch.what: Day 2 onwards: one way a day at most. The Frostline (45 minutes of rest in all) and Cogsworth (one rest of 30 minutes) usually open on days 2 and 3. The Brackens and the Lull are open from the start, so the drover's and the bargee's chapters run alongside. The first apprentice usually joins in the first week: when the gardener's story ends Cairn wakes, and the stone circle calls the two valley folk not chosen at the start.
firstLaunch.line: the high path is clear. no rush. it'll still be there.

home.about: The home base from PR #146 (a proposal), in its Dream-Dust-only form (choices page, decision on materials): the hearth is the home's level and opens room to grow; a job is paid when queued and finishes after that many minutes of rest. Nothing is lost, nothing decays here, raids never touch it.

journeyEnd.what: When the stargazer's story ends, Mote joins as the fourteenth folk: the fourteenth stone in the woodland circle and the last crystal spire round the Dream Grove light, and the moon is full. Nothing more is asked; stories, comforts and the home carry on at the player's pace, and later regions bring new ways.
